The smallest, in the accent color, stays above 0 because the cycle's direction cannot be undone; ignoring direction (q = 0) gives 0, 1.5 and 1.5." width="100%"} The eigenvalues of `magnetic_laplacian_matrix()`, in increasing order. They are real because the matrix is Hermitian, and non-negative. The smallest is `0` when the phases around every cycle cancel out, as on a graph whose undirected version is a forest or whose edges are all two-way, so it measures how far the edge directions are from being consistent: for example, a directed cycle of length `L` keeps it above `0` unless `qL` is a whole number. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.25]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The charge, between `0` and `0.5`. Default is `0.25`. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use the normalized magnetic Laplacian, whose eigenvalues lie in $[0, 2]$. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The eigenvalues in increasing order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or `q` is not between `0` and `0.5`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The dense Hermitian matrix is fully diagonalized, $O(V^3)$ time. Matches NetworkX's `magnetic_spectrum()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a directed triangle the phases at `q = 0.25` add up to three quarter turns, so `0` is not an eigenvalue; at `q = 0` the spectrum is that of the undirected triangle (with edge weights halved, as $W'$ averages the two directions): ::: {#c34ace05 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_cycle_graph(3) ( [round(v, 3) + 0.0 for v in cycle.magnetic_spectrum()], [round(v, 3) + 0.0 for v in cycle.magnetic_spectrum(q=0)], ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([0.134, 1.0, 1.866], [0.0, 1.5, 1.5]) ``` ::: :::
